Extensively researched, leaves nary a stone unturned, with a distinct bent toward the British palate, Robert Massie's dreadnought is worth the read. My only real concern is that the book suffers from the title, as it has very little to do with said vessels, but more to do with the naval philosophy of Great Britain. I am currently reading Massie's "Castles of Steel" as per the suggestion of another reviewer... First read Dreanought, and then read Castles of Steel in order to get a better appreciation of the philosophies that directed the historical construction, and confrontation between the navies of Great Britain and the Imperial German High Seas Fleet.
